Give this plan 30 days. Track what you eat, maintain a sensible calorie deficit, prioritize protein and fiber, eat healthy fats, lift weights, walk, sleep, hydrate, and stay consistent. You don’t need some crazy starvation diet or hours of cardio.

1. Track Your Calories. If you’re not tracking what you eat, you’re guessing. I actually use ChatGPT to keep a running total of my calories and macros throughout the day. First, determine approximately how many calories you need to maintain your weight. For me, at around 150 pounds, that’s roughly 2,400 calories. To lose body fat, I eat about 400 calories below maintenance. Don’t just slash calories dramatically—the goal is to lose fat while preserving muscle, not simply make the number on the scale drop.

2. Prioritize Protein. I’m shooting for roughly .7 to 1 gram of protein per pound of body weight, and personally, I’m getting around 150 grams a day. Protein helps preserve muscle when you’re in a caloric deficit, and it also keeps you fuller longer. Eggs, cottage cheese, chicken, lean beef, bison, and fish are some of my favorites.

3. Don’t Be Afraid of Healthy Fats. One of the biggest changes I made was actually increasing my fat consumption. I’m talking about healthy fats from foods like salmon, avocado, nuts, legumes, and olive oil. I eat an avocado every day, consume plenty of nuts and fish, and take omega-3 supplements. My dietary fat went up while my body fat went down.

4. Get Your Fiber. I’m aiming for around 30–40 grams of fiber a day. Fiber helps keep you full, and I get mine from foods like avocados, sweet potatoes, barley, whole grains, and vegetables, along with psyllium husk. Another reason I focus on fiber is how it affects my glucose response when I eat carbohydrates.

5. Change the Order You Eat Your Food. This was a freaking game-changer for me. I start with fiber—something like a green salad—then eat my protein and fat, and save my carbohydrates for last. I started experimenting with this after reading The Glucose Revolution and wearing a continuous glucose monitor for 21 days. I was blown away by the changes in my body composition. I wasn’t necessarily changing what I ate; I changed the order I ate it, and I started getting incredibly lean.

6. Keep Lifting Heavy. Do not stop lifting weights when you’re trying to lose fat! Get your ass in the gym consistently and challenge your muscles. I lift heavy but controlled because I want to give my body every reason possible to preserve muscle while I’m in a caloric deficit—and potentially even build some.

7. Walk More. I walk about 8,000–12,000 steps every day. Interestingly, when I backed off running and high-intensity StairMaster sessions and focused more on walking, my body fat dropped. If you want to crank things up, try incline treadmill walking. I like around 3 mph at a 12% incline for 30–60 minutes.

8. Stop Eating at Night. This was another big change for me because I used to snack at night. Now, I try to finish eating by around 7:00 p.m., and then I’m done. No random snacking or mindlessly eating later in the evening. For me, making that change has been incredibly effective.

9. Prioritize Sleep. You cannot overlook recovery. Sleep gives your body an opportunity to heal and recover, and I consider getting roughly 7–9 hours a night non-negotiable.

10. Stop Drinking Your Calories. Soda, sweet tea, sugary coffee drinks, beer, alcohol—cut that crap out. Liquid calories can add up ridiculously fast without filling you up. Instead, I prioritize water. I personally shoot for around 120 ounces a day and carry a giant insulated bottle around because it makes staying hydrated incredibly easy.

11. Be Patient. This is probably the most important part. You cannot control exactly where your body loses fat first. You might notice your face getting leaner, then your chest, upper abs, lower abs, obliques, and eventually those stubborn areas around your back and love handles. Don’t get discouraged because the area you want gone the most is taking the longest.

A lot of guys assume they can tell how high their testosterone is just by looking in the mirror. Big beard? High testosterone. Bald? High testosterone. Deep voice, big hands, broad shoulders? Same assumption. But the more I’ve researched testosterone, the more I’ve realized it’s not that simple.You cannot accurately determine your testosterone level by looking at yourself. You can have every one of these signs—or none of them—and still not know what’s actually happening hormonally. The only real way to know is through blood work. I recommend getting tested regularly so you have a baseline and can see how your levels change over time. That gives you an opportunity to address your lifestyle, training, nutrition, sleep, and recovery before low testosterone becomes a bigger problem.

A lot of physical characteristics are influenced by genetics and the testosterone you were exposed to during puberty—not necessarily what your testosterone levels look like today. There are, however, some signs that can indicate your testosterone is still healthy and exactly where it needs to be:

You build and maintain muscle relatively easily. Testosterone supports muscle protein synthesis, so having adequate levels can make it easier to maintain and build muscle. But testosterone is only part of the equation—your nutrition, workouts, sleep, and recovery matter too.

You’re strong for your size. If you’re naturally strong relative to your body weight, can train hard, and have good physical performance and endurance, that can be another positive sign. Testosterone affects muscle mass, recovery, and neuromuscular function.

Your libido and sexual function are strong. If you’re thinking about sex, have a healthy sex drive, and don’t have problems performing, chances are your testosterone is doing pretty well. One of the things that can happen when testosterone declines is a noticeable drop in libido and sexual performance.

You have oily skin or still get pimples. This may not be the testosterone superpower you were hoping for, but androgens can stimulate your sebaceous glands to produce more oil. That’s also why some guys who start using testosterone can experience acne.

Your body and facial hair haven’t thinned significantly. Having a thick beard doesn’t automatically mean your testosterone is high today, but if you developed a lot of body or facial hair when you were younger and it remains thick as you age, that can be a positive indicator. Genetics and androgen sensitivity also play a major role.

You maintain a masculine physique. Broad shoulders, a smaller waist, and the ability to carry and maintain muscle can be associated with adequate testosterone. As testosterone declines with age, guys may find it harder to maintain muscle and easier to gain body fat.

With high testosterone, what about hair LOSS? A testosterone-related issue we need to talk about is hair loss. Having high testosterone doesn’t automatically mean you’re going bald. Male pattern hair loss has a lot to do with DHT (dihydrotestosterone) and how genetically sensitive your hair follicles are to it. Testosterone can be converted into DHT, which can gradually miniaturize susceptible follicles until the hair eventually falls out. This is actually one of the reasons we developed Pete & Pedro’s new DHT Defense Shampoo. I was worried about keeping my own hair, and I wanted something designed to support healthier hair and scalp. We spent nine months developing it with ingredients including saw palmetto, pygeum, caffeine, biotin, green tea, zinc, B vitamins, and a ton of botanicals. We wanted to create a shampoo for guys noticing thinning—or those who want to be proactive about caring for the hair they’ve got.

items.title: 1,000 People a Day!! 🦞 Toronto's Legendary Lobster Restaurant!
items.summary: Will we be able to finish an 18-pound lobster tower? Welcome to Fishman Lobster Clubhouse in Toronto, Canada — one of the most famous and iconic Chinese
items.text:
Will we be able to finish an 18-pound lobster tower? Welcome to Fishman Lobster Clubhouse in Toronto, Canada — one of the most famous and iconic Chinese seafood restaurants in the world!

Serving over 1,000 people a day, this legendary restaurant is world-renowned for its massive, mountain-high towers of Hong Kong-style fried lobster piled high with fried garlic.

Joined by Toronto food insider Clement Leung (@InstaNoodls) we sit down with owner Ray to learn how a small, struggling strip-mall Cantonese restaurant, that didn't even originally serve seafood, transformed into a global seafood phenomenon.

Before diving into the main event, we get rare kitchen access to see their incredible dry-aging program and try dishes you would never guess they serve here — including a mouthwatering 20-Day Dry-Aged AAA Canadian Ribeye and fresh Steamed Green Bass!

Then comes the ultimate climax: pulling two massive live Canadian lobsters weighing in at 18 pounds, frying them in high-heat woks with a mountain of garlic, and building the famous Hong Kong Style Lobster Tower!

📍 RESTAURANT LOCATION & FEATURED DISHES

Fishman Lobster Clubhouse
🔗 Google Maps: https://maps.app.goo.gl/FishmanLobsterClubhouse

🍽️ Featured Dishes & Prices:
🥩 20-Day Dry-Aged AAA Canadian Ribeye ($100 CAD) – A surprising house specialty dry-aged in-house and cooked over high-heat woks.
🐟 Steamed Green Bass ($35/lb CAD) – Classic Cantonese-style fresh fish steamed with ginger, scallions, and soy sauce.
🦞 18 lbs Canadian Lobster Tower (HK Style) ($35/lb CAD) – Two giant lobsters fried to perfection, stacked into a sky-high tower, and buried in crispy fried garlic!

items.title: Afghanistan is DANGEROUS for Food Lovers!! 🇦🇫 (Kabul's Best Street Food)
items.summary: Today we're going on an ultimate Afghanistan street food tour in Kabul! Kabul is the biggest, liveliest, and most surprising city in Afghanistan, and today
items.text:
Today we're going on an ultimate Afghanistan street food tour in Kabul! Kabul is the biggest, liveliest, and most surprising city in Afghanistan, and today we’re exploring a side of this country that most people outside rarely get to see—incredible food, ancient traditions, and mind-blowing hospitality.

Today, our local friend Bilal (https://www.instagram.com/bilalkwardak ) along with my friend Jon (🎥 https://www.instagram.com/jontravelist/ ), are going deep into the heart of the Kabul for a full-day street food marathon. We start our morning with rich, creamy Qaymaq (Afghan clotted cream) before diving into Kabul's busiest street markets for handmade cheese, steamed Mantu dumplings, and comforting Aush noodles.

We'll also wander through Ka Faroshi, Kabul's famous 200-year-old bird market, grab some street-side liver and tripe, and taste Chainaki—a classic lamb and chickpea stew slow-cooked inside ceramic teapots.

After washing it down with fresh pomegranate juice and crispy stuffed Bolani flatbread, we finish the night at Super Shinwari for an epic feast of Shinwari White Lamb Karahi and melt-in-your-mouth Dampokht lamb.

📍 THE KABUL STREET FOOD TOUR
🫓 Watani Breakfast Shop – Fresh Afghan Qaymaq (clotted cream) & hot naan
🥟 Kabul Old City Market – Street-cart hard cheese, Mantu (dumplings) & Aush noodle stew
🐦 Ka Faroshi Bird Market – Historic 200-year-old alleyway & street-side Liver and Tripe
🫖 Wahid Restaurant – Traditional teapot-cooked Chainaki lamb stew
🥤 Street Food Stalls – Fresh pomegranate juice, chickpeas & crispy stuffed Bolani
🥩 Super Shinwari Restaurant – Shinwari White Lamb Karahi & Dampokht pressure-cooked lamb

Have you ever tried Afghan food? Let me know in the comments which dish you'd try first!

Thanks to Bilal ( https://www.instagram.com/bilalkwardak ) for arranging our trip to Afghanistan.

items.title: Anthropic blocks possible attempt to use AI to make biological weapons
items.summary: Anthropic says it has identified and disrupted attempts to use its AI model for "malicious activity" which could support the development of biological
items.text:
Anthropic says it has identified and disrupted attempts to use its AI model for "malicious activity" which could support the development of biological weapons.

The findings, made in the firm's recent threat intelligence report, is the latest in a growing series of warnings from AI researchers and industry insiders about the technology's potential risks to humanity.

The warnings have prompted calls to action, with US Senator Bernie Sanders demanding a pause on advanced AI development and a ban on artificial superintelligence.

President Donald Trump has so far rejected such fears, saying on Thursday he was concerned "if we don't win AI, we're going to be put in a very bad position".

The company published its latest threat intelligence report, external on Thursday.

Such reports have become a regular feature across the AI industry as firms seek to demonstrate how they identify and disrupt attempts to misuse their models.

This includes Google, which wrote on Tuesday, external that a person had attempted to use its AI tool, Gemini, to obtain a "complete, step-by-step technical guide for synthesizing weaponised biological agents".

Claude, Anthropic's AI model was also used by actors linked to a Russia-based cyber espionage campaign and by an Iranian propaganda institution, according to its report.

The cases of concern detected over the past eight months ranged from fake dating apps and hotel Wifi scams, to surveillance built to identify dissidents.

Anthropic has also accused Chinese AI firms of trying to replicate Claude's capabilities.

The lengthy report lists cases in which suspected state-sponsored groups, criminals, spyware vendors, state propaganda institutions and politically motivated individuals misused its technology.

"Malicious use" of its Claude Haiku, Sonnet, and Opus models was disrupted between December 2025 and August 2026, it said.

None of the misuse cases involved Claude Fable or the powerful Mythos-class models, with the exception of one instance of distillation - the process for training smaller AI models using larger, more expensive models.

As well as detecting the use of its models for cyber and influence operations, surveillance, scams and fraud and weapon development, Anthropic said it had blocked scientists who used its AI in ways that could support biological weapons development.

The report highlighted "five case studies of actors using our models in ways that could support biological weapons development".

Biological misuse, it said, is "one of the most serious risks of frontier AI model". Without the correct safeguards, such capabilities "could have catastrophic consequences", Anthropic said.

"The same information that can be used to develop a biological weapon could also be used to develop, for example, a vaccine or a cure for a disease," Anthropic said.

Jacob Klein, the head of threat intelligence at Anthropic, told the New York Times, external it was "an incredibly nuanced situation".

"You are not seeing someone in a comic book kind of way say, 'Hey, I want to build a biological weapon to kill everybody,'" he said.

The report also noted six cases where Claude was used "to develop software for conventional weapons, including firearms, missiles, armed drones, bombs, and other munitions, as well as the targeting and control systems that operate them".

The report indicated that cybercriminals and state-backed hackers have increasingly used its technology to assist their operations.

Hacking group ShinyHunters, as well as China-based labs, were among those named in the report.

The report also said that a hacking group whose work is consistent with the Russia-based Midnight Blizzard allegedly used AI to build a system that automatically detected when its malware was flagged by security defences and rewrote code until it evaded detection.

The California-based company said it had incorporated its findings into its processes "to better prevent, detect, and disrupt these activities in the future".

Anthropic said it had shared intelligence with authorities and industry partners where appropriate.

The report - the company's first this year - comes after a top safety researcher at Anthropic warned AI is advancing so quickly he believes there is a greater than 10% chance it "could kill all humans" within the next decade.

In an article published on 6 September, OpenAI chief scientist Jakub Pachocki called for the industry to implement "voluntary slowdowns" until safeguards are set.

"I am concerned no one is prepared for the consequences of a continued rapid rise in machine intelligence," Pachocki said, adding that OpenAI, which makes ChatGPT, will continue its work on building safeguards, though broader interventions are required.

The warning prompted an open letter to UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham calling for a new multinational treaty for the safe development of AI and a call for governments to collaborate about what a treaty based on the development of superintelligence should look like.

In the US, Democratic lawmaker Bernie Sanders has introduced legislation to ban AI superintelligence and temporarily pause advanced AI development.

"When scientists tell you there is a chance, a chance that it could have a cataclysmic impact on humanity, you've got be a moron not to say, slow it down," he said on Thursday on BBC's Newsnight.

With additional reporting from Osmond Chia.

items.text:
Israel's military says it has destroyed a large underground complex operated by Hezbollah in southern Lebanon.

It said it used more than 1,000 tonnes of explosives to destroy two tunnels spanning more than 2km (1.2 miles) beneath the Ali Taher Ridge.

The blast triggered seismic activity equivalent to a magnitude 4.1 earthquake, according to the US Geological Survey.

There was no immediate public response from Hezbollah or the Lebanese government.

Israeli forces took control of the ridge last week after months of fighting with the Iran-backed group there. The Israeli military occupies a large swathe of southern Lebanon captured after the conflict with Hezbollah resumed in March.

Images released by the Israel Defense Forces (IDF) showed a fireball lighting up the sky.

"The sky lit up and about 15 seconds later we heard the terrifying sound," Ahamed, a resident in Nabatieh, about 6km west of the ridge, told the BBC.

"The house shook all together as if it was literally an earthquake."

He said people were screaming and children were crying, and that cars filled the roads as people left the area for Beirut.

Tremors were even felt in the coastal city of Saida 40km north.

The IDF said the underground infrastructure included a command centre used by Hezbollah's Badr unit and contained dozens of rockets, missiles and unmanned aerial vehicles, as well as anti-tank weapons, mines and explosives.

"This was strategic infrastructure that was constructed over two decades, funded and planned by the Iranian terror regime," the IDF said in a statement on Telegram.

"All of the terrorists who were inside the infrastructure were eliminated or fled."

The IDF said the destruction of the complex completed a mission to destroy eight tunnels and establish a "security zone" in the area.

The latest action comes amid renewed fighting in southern Lebanon, where Israeli forces have expanded operations against Hezbollah positions and continue to hold what Israel describes as a security zone near the border.

Lebanese media reported fresh Israeli strikes elsewhere in the south on Thursday, including Nabatieh al-Fawqa and Mansouri in the Tyre district.

The Lebanese army has increased deployments in areas outside Israeli control, including the southern city of Nabatieh, in efforts to strengthen stability and reassure residents, local television station MTV reported.

Lebanon was drawn into the war between Israel, the US and Iran on 2 March, when Hezbollah launched rockets into Israel in retaliation for a strike that killed Iran's supreme leader.

Israel responded by launching a bombing campaign across Lebanon and invading a significant part of the country's south. Its forces continue to occupy roughly 5% of Lebanese territory.

Fighting decreased following a ceasefire deal between Iran and the US in June, alongside a separate agreement between Lebanon and Israel. While hundreds of thousands of people have returned to their homes in Lebanon in the last few months, about 330,000 remain displaced as a result of the conflict, according to the United Nations.

Under the Lebanon-Israel framework, Hezbollah is expected to disarm, Israeli forces to withdraw gradually from southern Lebanon and the Lebanese army to deploy across the area.

Hezbollah was not directly involved in the agreement and has rejected direct negotiations.

Despite a reduction in fighting, Israeli strikes and demolitions in southern Lebanon have continued.

At least 4,383 people - including 395 women and 259 children - have been killed in Lebanon by Israeli attacks since 2 March, according to the health ministry, whose figures do not differentiate between combatants and civilians. At least 29 have been killed this week, the ministry says.

Israeli authorities say 40 Israeli soldiers and four civilians have been killed in the same period.

Additional reporting by Raffi Berg in London and Samantha Granville and Ghaith Solh in Beirut
